planner_json.title: Remove T16's verify declaration and write allow-list, and admit node scripts on claude-code

write_prohibited: test/harness/graders/** - E1 and E2 own grading and the report writer
plugins/pixel-perfect/** - no plugin change in this task
.github/workflows/harness-eval.yml - no workflow change in this task
Any file not listed in WRITE-ALLOWED

seed/real-run-dirs.description: Real run directories from prepareVerifyPair and prepareRunDirs over the real case manifests

seed/keyless-claude-cli.description: The real claude CLI on the host, started from an empty env plus an allowlist, with a temp HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL at a closed local port, and a literal placeholder key
records: the CLI's init event arrives with no model request

specification.objective: A claude-code verify invocation is told nothing about a report and can write nothing by rule, and every claude-code graded run may execute node scripts.
specification.success_state: Verify prompts read `/pixel-perfect:verify --platform web-desktop`. Each graded argv ends with `--allowedTools Bash(node *)`, and no recorded argv holds `Edit(`. `VERIFY_REPORT_CONTRACT`, `verifyReportPrompt` and `allowed_writes` are gone. The status prompt still holds `Phase:`, and T16's status assertions are unchanged.

requirements.description: GIVEN real run directories from `prepareVerifyPair` and `prepareRunDirs` over the real case manifests WHEN the verify pair and the invocation table are built, and each graded entry's prompt and `bound_path` are read THEN the planted and clean prompts each equal `/pixel-perfect:verify --platform web-desktop`, the status-a prompt holds `Phase:`, and each verify `bound_path` ends with its case's `report_relative_path` under its own run directory
requirements.verification_service: real invocation table, case manifests and run directories
requirements.positive_example: The planted and clean prompts each read exactly /pixel-perfect:verify --platform web-desktop, the status-a prompt still holds Phase:, and each verify entry's bound_path sits under its own run directory.
requirements.red: On base the planted verify prompt names reports/verify-button-drift.json and the invocation id, so the first assertion fails.

scenario.verification_service: real invocation table, case manifests and run directories

would_fail_if: verifyReportPrompt is still appended, so a verify prompt names the report path
the status surface is removed with the verify half
bound_path is removed, so E2 has nowhere to write

build_proof.range: anything that proves a graded verify run is never told to write a report, while status keeps its surface and the report path stays bound
examples: promptFor composing only the status surface

steps: build the verify pair and the invocation table over the real manifests
read each graded entry's prompt and bound_path

must_observe: the planted and clean `prompt` each equal `/pixel-perfect:verify --platform web-desktop`
each verify `bound_path` ends with its case's `report_relative_path` under its own run directory
must_not_observe: the entry's `invocation_id` in a verify prompt
an empty prompt on any graded entry

requirements.description: GIVEN the real claude CLI with an empty env plus an allowlist, a temp HOME, a closed local endpoint and a placeholder key WHEN each graded entry's argv is read, the CLI starts with the status entry's flags until its init event, and a recorded stance is edited to hold each of `Edit(reports/a.json)`, `Bash(*)` and `Bash` THEN each of the 4 graded argv holds `--allowedTools` `Bash(node *)`, the init event reads `permissionMode` `dontAsk`, and each edited stance throws `stance-argv-not-approved`
requirements.verification_service: real claude CLI with an empty env, a closed local endpoint and a placeholder key
requirements.positive_example: Each graded entry's argv ends with --allowedTools Bash(node *), the real CLI's init event reads permissionMode dontAsk with those flags, and a recorded stance edited to hold Edit(reports/a.json), Bash(*) or Bash is refused.
requirements.red: On base a stance with no declared write has no --allowedTools, so the argv assertion fails.

scenario.verification_service: real claude CLI with an empty env, a closed local endpoint and a placeholder key

would_fail_if: the node rule is omitted from the row
the exact argv comparison is removed, so a wider rule is admitted
the write list is left in place, so an Edit rule still reaches the argv

build_proof.range: anything that proves every claude-code stance holds exactly the node rule, and that the CLI starts with it

steps: read each graded entry's argv from the real table
start the real CLI with the status entry's own flags, read its init event, then stop it
edit a recorded stance's argv to hold each of `Edit(reports/a.json)`, `Bash(*)` and `Bash`, then call assertStance

must_observe: each of the 4 graded argv holds `--allowedTools` `Bash(node *)`
each of the 3 edited stances throws `stance-argv-not-approved`
must_not_observe: an empty argv on a graded entry
